summary: The six cases are real tests, not coverage: the one-url fake plus the exact-url assertion genuinely closes criterion 4's locally-constructed-grant defect, and criterion 5's swallow defect dies on a measured mutation. What is unconstrained is the OTHER half of the new bytesOf branch -- no test ever gives a ConsumerClient a SegmentSource and then pushes a non-DIRECT delivery, so hoisting the null-source check above the via check survives the entire 1287-test suite while every inline delivery would issue a consumer-side GET.

findings.title: Nothing constrains that the seam is NOT used when via is not DIRECT
The grant-on-non-DIRECT guard is asserted for INLINE only; PROXY is unconstrained
The grant binding is pinned for the FIRST delivery only, not per-delivery
